name: Matthew Rankin
bio: Matthew Rankin (born August 5, 1980; Winnipeg) is a Canadian experimental filmmaker.

credits.title: Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney
credits.overview: Via archival footage and a vintage yet unserious style, this is the hot-shot, right-wing, weird and wild story of Canada's Progressive Conservatives, told through the journey of 18th Prime Minister Brian Mulroney's career as a Tory hopeful to the day of his inauguration.

credits.title: So Long Pluto
credits.overview: In space, a charming little planet named Pluto dreams of joining the Solar System’s official dance troupe. With the help of her asteroid friend, Ceres, and her human discoverer, Clyde William Tombaugh, she will do everything she can to make it happen. credits.title: Blue Heron
credits.overview: A family of six's fresh start on 1990s Vancouver Island unravels as their youngest child, Sasha, witnesses the increasingly dangerous behavior of her older brother, Jeremy.

credits.title: Le Tour De Canada
credits.overview: Two cyclists face off in a brutal cross Canada bike race.

credits.title: Universal Language
credits.overview: Winter. Somewhere between Tehran and Winnipeg. Negin and Nazgol find a sum of money frozen deep within the sidewalk ice and try to find a way to get it out. credits.title: Before I Change My Mind
credits.overview: 1987: While the other students wonder if new kid Robin is a boy or a girl, Robin forges a complicated bond with the school bully, making increasingly dangerous choices to fit in.

credits.title: Federal Owl Commission
credits.overview: A demented parody of the Canadian government.

credits.title: Mademoiselle Kenopsia
credits.overview: Set on carrying out her task with dedication, a woman is obsessed with watching over anonymous interiors and occupying them. Both a custodian of the premises and a ghostly presence, she becomes an echo of how we relate to time, solitude and the melancholy of forsaken spaces.

credits.title: This House
credits.overview: Bridgeport, January 17, 2008. A teenage girl is found hanged in her room. While everything points to suicide, the autopsy report reveals something else. credits.title: You Are in Bear Country 1
credits.overview: 16mm dreamwave micro-hallucinations in National Parks across Canada.

credits.title: You Are in Bear Country 5
credits.overview: Another chapter of the 16mm dreamwave micro-hallucinations in National Parks across Canada.

credits.title: A Grief Observed
credits.overview: Matthew spends Mother’s Day in his mom’s house slowly deleting her voicemails.

credits.title: The Twentieth Century
credits.overview: Toronto, Canada, 1899. William Lyon Mackenzie King (1874-1950) fervently believes that he is destined to become Prime Minister, but to do so he will first have to fight his personal obsessions and overcome the many obstacles he will encounter on his tortuous path to power.

credits.title: Wilcox
credits.overview: Wilcox exists outside the norm. Deserter, delinquent, or survivalist, he quietly roams, looking to put down roots or for what could simply be called freedom.

credits.title: A Fortress
credits.overview: After the death of their adoptive daughter a couple goes to Haiti. There, they meet with a DNA specialist who has the power of resurrection.

credits.title: The Tesla World Light
credits.overview: New York, 1905. Visionary inventor Nikola Tesla makes one last appeal to J.P. Morgan, his onetime benefactor.

credits.title: This Is an Official Message
credits.overview: In the idealism and mutation of his home town of Winnipeg, the filmmaker Matthew Rankin launches a failed campaign of absolute inter-human solidarity entirely in Esperanto, the artificial language of world peace.

credits.title: The Radical Expeditions of Walter Boudreau
credits.overview: This micro-epic short film is an inspired tribute to visionary avant-garde composer Walter Boudreau: his life, work, mischief, and boundless artistic curiosity. credits.title: Mynarski Death Plummet
credits.overview: A completely hand-made historical micro-epic about the final minutes in the life of Winnipeg's doomed Second World War hero, Andrew Mynarski (1916-1944). credits.title: Tabula Rasa
credits.overview: In the aftermath of the 1950 Winnipeg flood, Fernand floats listlessly through the sad, sunken landscape of ruin. His estranged wife prays for the drowned souls of Saint-Boniface.

credits.title: Kubasa in a Glass: The Fetishised Winnipeg TV Commercial 1976-1992
credits.overview: Originally released in 2006, Kubasa in a Glass presents a digitally warped reflection of Winnipeg’s brief and disposable self-image, as seen through local no-budget and public access television of the 1980s.

credits.title: Laurentia
credits.overview: A young quebecer descends into alienation and depression.

credits.title: Negativipeg
credits.overview: An examination of Rory Lepine, who sent Winnipeg into a frenzy when he beat local legend Burton Cummings with a beer bottle in a 7-Eleven in 1985

credits.title: Hydro-Lévesque
credits.overview: Only the electrifying courage and love of Québec nationalism can save the citizens of Winnipeg from committing mass suicide.

credits.title: Barber Gull Rub

credits.overview: An experimental montage of the exteriors of apartment buildings

credits.title: The Phantom of the Cinematheque
credits.overview: On the 25th anniversary of his employment, Dave Barber, the visionary workaholic programmer of Winnipeg's beloved Cinematheque, dies tragically in an avalanche of VHS tapes while working late to finish the programming calendar. credits.title: Self-Portrait
credits.overview: Commissioned self-portrait of the artist as metaphysical remix of Abbas Kiarostami's "Close-Up" recorded on a cellphone.

credits.title: Discount Everything
credits.overview: Found-footage tribute to Winnipeg salesman and video artist Nick Hill.

credits.title: Où est Maurice?
credits.overview: On a moonlit street corner, a Parisian waif sits dejectedly on a doorstep, mournfully clutching a dogless leash.

credits.title: Kubasa in a Glass: The Strange World of the Winnipeg Television Commercial (1975-1993)
credits.overview: A found footage video essay tracing Winnipeg's civic pathologies, aesthetic fabulations and exquisite strangeness through the prism of its own low-budget, lo-fi TV advertising produced between 1975 and 1992.

credits.title: Death by Popcorn: The Tragedy of the Winnipeg Jets
credits.overview: A bizarre video collage created from the ashes of Winnipeg's local television broadcasts of decades past, detailing the rise and fall of the Winnipeg Jets.

credits.title: The Octopus Factor
credits.overview: A man confronts painful memories of a love affair now over. But he is perplexed by the appearance of a disgusting creature that he just can't get rid of. But can one really release oneself from the abominable things that haunt us?
